cases.subtitle: Rare genetic epilepsy linked to changes in the SCN2A sodium-channel gene
cases.overview: SCN2A-related disorders can look very different from one child to another. A key research clue is whether the variant increases or reduces sodium-channel activity, because that can change which related diseases and treatment strategies are most relevant.
current_landscape: Seizure treatments exist, but there is no approved therapy that directly corrects SCN2A itself.
Gain-of-function and loss-of-function variants can behave differently, so variant function matters.
Natural-history studies and patient registries are already building trial-readiness data.

matches.name: SCN8A-related epilepsy
matches.summary: Both can involve gain-of-function sodium-channel activity and very early epilepsy. This makes SCN8A the closest research match in this demo.

matches.name: SCN3A-related epilepsy
matches.summary: SCN3A can share the same broad sodium-channel gain-of-function pattern, but the clinical evidence base is smaller than for SCN8A.

matches.name: Dravet syndrome
matches.summary: Dravet syndrome shares epilepsy symptoms and the sodium-channel family, but its usual mechanism differs. That lowers the match despite the similar symptoms.

treatment_path.title: Sodium-channel blocking strategy
treatment_path.summary: For gain-of-function disease, both SCN2A and SCN8A can involve excessive sodium-channel activity. Published evidence in both disorders supports investigating sodium-channel blocking strategies.
transferable: The treatment-class rationale: reduce excessive sodium-channel activity.
Seizure-response and tolerability outcomes used to evaluate the strategy.
Trial-design lessons from related sodium-channel disorders.
not_transferable: A specific medicine or dose for an individual child.
The strategy if the SCN2A variant is loss-of-function or function is unknown.
Expected response for a particular patient without specialist review.
treatment_path.expert_note: Expert validation required: confirm the child's variant function and clinical phenotype before any clinical decision.

cases.subtitle: A genetic RAS/MAPK pathway disorder affecting development and multiple organ systems
cases.overview: Noonan syndrome belongs to a family of disorders called RASopathies. Several differently named syndromes disrupt the same RAS/MAPK growth-signaling pathway, which creates opportunities to compare research and targeted-treatment ideas across diseases.
current_landscape: Care is usually tailored to the person's specific heart, growth, developmental, or other features.
No single disease-modifying treatment applies to every person with Noonan syndrome.
Pathway-targeted therapies are being studied for selected severe RASopathy manifestations.

matches.name: Costello syndrome
matches.summary: Costello syndrome affects the same RAS/MAPK pathway and shares several developmental and cardiac features with Noonan syndrome.

matches.name: Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome
matches.summary: CFC syndrome is another RASopathy with strong pathway overlap and related developmental and cardiac manifestations.

matches.name: Neurofibromatosis type 1
matches.summary: NF1 also alters RAS/MAPK signaling, but its major clinical features differ more substantially from Noonan syndrome.

treatment_path.title: MEK-pathway inhibition for severe RASopathy-associated cardiomyopathy
treatment_path.summary: MEK inhibitors have been explored across several RASopathies for severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The shared pathway provides a rationale, but the evidence is still based on small numbers and specific manifestations.
transferable: The pathway rationale for studying MEK inhibition in severe RASopathy-associated cardiomyopathy.
Cardiac outcome measures and monitoring approaches used across related syndromes.
Cross-disease trial-design lessons for small rare-disease populations.
not_transferable: Using MEK inhibition as a general treatment for Noonan syndrome.
A specific drug, dose, or duration for an individual patient.
Evidence from one RASopathy without checking the exact gene, phenotype, and cardiac condition.
treatment_path.expert_note: Expert validation required: this research path is relevant only to selected severe manifestations and requires specialist evaluation.
